name: AMPSphere_search_amps
description: Filter/search the AMPSphere catalogue (863,498 prokaryotic smORF antimicrobial peptides from the 2024 Global Microbial smORF Catalogue, Big Data Biology Lab) by habitat, SPHERE family, microbial source, peptide length, molecular weight, isoelectric point, charge, and quality-control flags (exp_evidence, antifam, RNAcode, coordinates), with pagination. Returns a paginated list of AMPs, each with its accession, amino-acid sequence, physicochemical properties (length, MW, pI, charge, aromaticity, instability index, GRAVY) and quality flags. Interval filters use a 'min,max' string (e.g. pep_length_interval='8,20'). Set list_options=true to instead return the valid filter values (habitats, microbial sources, quality labels, and min/max ranges) from /v1/all_available_options. Keyless AMPSphere REST API.

list_options.description: If true, ignore all other filters and return the valid filter enumerations from /v1/all_available_options (quality labels, habitat list, microbial_source list, and min/max ranges for pep_length, molecular_weight, isoelectric_point, charge_at_pH_7). Use this first to discover valid habitat / microbial_source values.

habitat.description: Environmental habitat filter, e.g. 'human gut', 'soil', 'marine'. Must match an AMPSphere habitat label (see list_options).

family.description: SPHERE family accession filter, e.g. 'SPHERE-III.001_396'. Returns the AMPs in that family.

microbial_source.description: Microbial taxonomic source filter (GTDB-style name), e.g. 'Faecalibacterium'. See list_options for valid values.

exp_evidence.description: Experimental-evidence quality flag filter: 'Passed', 'Failed', or 'Not tested'.

antifam.description: Antifam quality flag filter: 'Passed', 'Failed', or 'Not tested' (Antifam = not a spurious/false ORF).

RNAcode.description: RNAcode coding-potential quality flag filter: 'Passed', 'Failed', or 'Not tested'.

coordinates.description: Genomic-coordinates quality flag filter: 'Passed', 'Failed', or 'Not tested'.

pep_length_interval.description: Peptide-length range as 'min,max' (residues), e.g. '8,20'. Catalogue range is 8-99.

mw_interval.description: Molecular-weight range as 'min,max' (Da), e.g. '800,3000'. Catalogue range is ~813-12286.

pI_interval.description: Isoelectric-point range as 'min,max', e.g. '9,12'. Catalogue range is ~4-12.

charge_interval.description: Net-charge-at-pH-7 range as 'min,max', e.g. '0,10'. Catalogue range is ~-57 to 44.

oneOf.description: List of AMP records (search), or the filter-options object (list_options).

sequence.description: The peptide sequence in one-letter code.

secondary_structure.description: Predicted secondary structure. Most antimicrobial peptides act as amphipathic helices, so a predicted helix is part of the case that the sequence is a real AMP.

family.description: The AMP family it was clustered into.

isoelectric_point.description: Isoelectric point. Antimicrobial peptides are typically cationic, so a low pI is unusual here.

charge.description: Net charge at neutral pH -- the property most AMP activity rests on.

gravy.description: Grand average of hydropathy. Together with `charge` it says whether the peptide can insert into a membrane.

instability_index.description: Predicted instability. Above 40 the peptide is predicted unstable in vitro.

coordinates.description: Where the gene sits in its source contig.

metadata.description: The sample and environment the peptide was found in.

num_genes.description: How many genes encode it across the catalogue. A peptide seen once is a singleton and may be a prediction artefact.

metaproteomes.description: Metaproteomic evidence that the peptide is actually translated -- the difference between a predicted ORF and an observed protein.

metatranscriptomes.description: Metatranscriptomic evidence that it is transcribed.

Antifam.description: Whether the sequence matches AntiFam, which flags spurious ORFs. A hit here means the 'peptide' is probably not real.

RNAcode.description: RNAcode's verdict on whether the ORF is protein-coding. The second independent check against a spurious call.

name: AMPSphere_get_family
description: Retrieve full detail for an AMPSphere protein family (SPHERE cluster) by accession (e.g. 'SPHERE-III.001_396'): the consensus sequence, member count, the full member-AMP accession list, per-member feature statistics, geographic / habitat / microbial-source distributions, and ready-to-use download URLs for the family's alignment (.aln), member sequences (.faa), HMM profile (.hmm), and phylogenetic tree (.nwk / ASCII figure). Keyless AMPSphere REST API (/v1/families/{accession}).

accession.description: SPHERE family accession. Example: 'SPHERE-III.001_396' (23 member AMPs, consensus 'GDKLXXXXXVDXXXXGGLIVKXGSRMXDXSLXXKLXXLXXAMKXXG').

name: AMPSphere_get_amp_distributions
description: Retrieve the ecological and geographic distribution of a single AMPSphere AMP by accession (e.g. 'AMP10.000_000'): where it has been observed as a bubble-map of lat/lon coordinates with sample counts, across which habitats, and from which microbial taxonomic sources. Returns three blocks: geo (type='bubble map' with parallel lat/lon/size arrays), habitat (labels + values), and microbial_source (labels + values). Keyless AMPSphere REST API (/v1/amps/{accession}/distributions).

name: AMPSphere_get_amp_features
description: Retrieve the full physicochemical feature profile of a single AMPSphere AMP by accession (e.g. 'AMP10.000_000'): molecular weight, length, molar extinction (reduced cysteines / cystine residues), aromaticity, GRAVY hydrophobicity, instability index, isoelectric point, net charge at pH 7, and predicted secondary-structure fractions (helix / turn / sheet). The same GRAVY / instability / pI / charge values are also available as fields on AMPSphere_search_amps; this tool adds molar extinction and secondary-structure fractions. Keyless AMPSphere REST API (/v1/amps/{accession}/features).

name: AMPSphere_get_statistics
description: Get AMPSphere's catalogue-wide totals from /v1/statistics: how many AMPs the resource holds (num_amps), how many predicted smORF genes they were called from (num_genes), how many SPHERE families they cluster into (num_families), and how many habitats, genomes and metagenomes they were surveyed across. Use it to size the resource before a filtered search, to report a denominator alongside a hit count, or to check whether a cached figure is still current -- the other AMPSphere tools quote 863,498 AMPs in their descriptions and that number comes from here. Takes no parameters. Keyless AMPSphere REST API.

num_genes.description: Predicted smORF genes the AMPs were called from.

num_families.description: SPHERE families the AMPs cluster into.

num_genomes.description: Genomes contributing at least one AMP.

num_metagenomes.description: Metagenomes contributing at least one AMP.
